verdict.rationale: GrowthBook documents official SDKs across the stack: a GitHub listing of 24 SDKs including Python, plus documented React/React Native, Vue, JS, Kotlin/Android, Swift/iOS and Flutter SDKs. Consistency is explicitly claimed: all SDKs share the same assignment logic and are backed by a 400+ test language-agnostic suite. The 2021 community remark about lacking native mobile SDKs is superseded by the current Kotlin and Swift SDK docs, so it is not a concrete contradiction. Missing for 10: independent or hands-on corroboration of cross-SDK consistency, backend SDK docs beyond a name in the GitHub list, and full feature parity across SDKs (streaming is JavaScript and React only).

support.subject: As a developer, I can use official SDKs across my whole stack — backend, web, and mobile — with consistent flag behavior

citations.quote: 24 SDKs including React, Python, Android, and iOS.
All SDKs use the same assignment logic, so the same attributes always produce the same variation regardless of which SDK you use.
an extensive test suite with over 400 language-agnostic unit tests in JSON format
Install the GrowthBook Kotlin SDK to evaluate feature flags and run A/B tests in Android apps using Android SDK 21 and above.
Install the GrowthBook Swift SDK to evaluate feature flags and run A/B tests on iOS, macOS, tvOS, and other Apple platforms.
This evaluation happens wherever the SDK runs—in the browser, on your server, or at the edge.
